brief.summary: I could not find a published count of 2025 arXiv papers on galaxy cluster physics, so the figure below is my own estimate, not a measured value. It is about 1,000 papers, with a plausible range of 700 to 1,500. The size of the field is reasonably well anchored. A blog post found through web search (not citable on its own) says the Open Journal of Astrophysics published 213 papers in 2025 and that this was 'only just over 1%' of astro-ph submissions. That implies roughly 213/0.011, or about 19,000 astro-ph papers in 2025 (range about 17,000 to 21,000). The share of those papers that are about galaxy clusters is the uncertain step. I assume it is about 4-6% when counting broadly: intracluster medium X-ray and SZ work, cluster cosmology and mass calibration, cluster lensing, radio halos and relics, AGN feedback in cool cores, cluster galaxy evolution and protoclusters, and cluster simulations. That gives about 750 to 1,150 papers, and I would round to about 1,000. A narrow definition (ICM and cluster physics only) could give about 500; counting every paper that merely mentions clusters could give 1,500 or more. Lewis, Shah and Alfred (arXiv:2602.12303) analysed every astro-ph paper from 2025, including keyword and subfield breakdowns. Its abstract does not give the totals, so its full text is the best place to replace both of my assumptions with measured numbers.

directions.goal: Produce a sourced, rough estimate of how many 2025 arXiv papers concern galaxy cluster physics, under a strict and a broad definition. Replace the survey's assumed 5-8% topic share and its unverified total astro-ph count with numbers quoted from papers wherever the literature allows.
directions.rationale: The survey estimate (about 1,500 strict, range 1,000-2,500; up to about 3,000 broad) rests on two weak inputs: an unverified web snippet for total astro-ph volume, and an assumed cluster share. 'Astrophysics Wrapped 2025' (2602.12303) and AstroMLab 5 (2511.12353) are full-text sources that may state both quantities directly, as a 2025 paper count and as subfield or concept statistics. With no ADS or arXiv-API counting tool available, this paper-based route is the most direct one. One direction is enough because both inputs come from the same few papers.
steps: Download the full text of arXiv:2602.12303 (Astrophysics Wrapped 2025). Read chunks to find (a) the total number of 2025 astro-ph papers, noting whether it counts primary-category papers only or includes cross-lists, and the split by subcategory (astro-ph.CO, astro-ph.GA, astro-ph.HE); (b) any topic, cluster or keyword statistics that mention galaxy clusters, the ICM, the SZ effect, cluster cosmology, protoclusters or radio halos. Use get_paper_figures only if the topic breakdown is given only in a figure, and record the figure number.

Download the full text of arXiv:2511.12353 (AstroMLab 5). Look for per-year paper counts (2020-2025) and any concept or topic-frequency tables that include galaxy clusters or the intracluster medium. Record the share of papers tagged with cluster-related concepts. If only the 1992-July 2025 aggregate exists, record it and note that it is an aggregate.

If neither paper gives a cluster share, look for an independent anchor. Use search_arxiv_abstracts and web_search for arXiv submission statistics (the arXiv annual report with astro-ph counts for 2024 or 2025) and for bibliometric studies of astro-ph topic distributions, such as subfield shares or extragalactic/cosmology topic modelling. Use get_arxiv_metadata to confirm IDs and dates.

Sanity-check the density of cluster papers. Run a handful of focused search_arxiv_abstracts queries ('galaxy cluster 2025', 'intracluster medium', 'protocluster JWST', 'radio halo relic LOFAR', 'eROSITA cluster cosmology', 'Sunyaev-Zeldovich cluster'). For each, note how many results fall in 2025 and whether they are galaxy-cluster papers rather than star clusters. Treat this as a qualitative check on topic breadth only, not as a count.

Combine the inputs: total 2025 astro-ph papers (with the cross-list caveat) times the strict cluster share, and times the broad share. Propagate the ranges on both factors. Where the share is still an assumption, label it as one and justify it from the closest sourced proxy, for example the astro-ph.CO plus astro-ph.GA fraction multiplied by a cluster fraction within those categories.
Cite every number used, with verbatim quotes, through cite(). Record clearly which inputs are sourced and which are assumed.
success_criteria: A sourced 2025 astro-ph total, with a quote and an explicit statement of whether cross-lists are included, or a documented dead end if the papers do not give one.
A cluster share taken from a quoted source, or explicitly marked as an assumption with a stated proxy.
A final strict estimate and a broad estimate, each with a range and a short calculation, and a note on whether the survey's central figure of about 1,500 survives.
At least two papers cited with validated verbatim quotes.

result.summary: Sourced base (f-001, high confidence): arXiv:2602.12303 (Astrophysics Wrapped 2025, Sec. 2.1) gives 18,660 astro-ph papers for 2025. Quote: 'This does not include replacement submissions ... The dataset also does not include cross-submissions'. The base is therefore primary-category papers only, which answers q-01. This is the low end of the survey's unverified 18,000-21,000. Sourced split (f-002, Table 1 of 2602.12303): GA 4,761; HE 3,869; SR 2,958; CO 2,789; EP 2,293; IM 1,722; general 268. GA plus CO is 40.5% of the total; GA plus CO plus HE is 61.2%. Neither 2602.12303 nor AstroMLab 5 (arXiv:2511.12353) gives a numerical galaxy-cluster share (dead end x-01). 2602.12303 gives keyword and subfield statistics only as figures. Its Figs. 12 and 13 were extracted to the run directory (/Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-features/runs/261015_224454/figures_2602.12303/) but not read numerically. 2511.12353 gives only example concepts and the aggregate for 1992 to July 2025, with no per-year counts. Its ADS keyword table lists 'galaxies: evolution' at 5.5% and 'dark matter' at 3.0%, with no cluster row. The cluster share is therefore still an assumption, applied per category on top of the sourced split (f-003, low confidence): CO 15-25%, GA 8-12%, HE 3-5%, other categories about 30-80 papers. That gives a strict estimate of about 950-1,550 papers, central about 1,200 (about 6.5% of 18,660). The broad estimate, which adds papers where clusters are a secondary topic plus gr-qc/hep-ph papers cross-listed into astro-ph, is about 2,000-3,000. The survey's central figure of about 1,500 survives, at the upper edge of the strict range; a central value near 1,200 is better supported by the confirmed primary-only base of 18,660. The abstract searches mostly returned galaxy-cluster papers but also star clusters, so keyword counts must exclude star clusters. Limitations: the full-text files are 2602.12303.txt and 2511.12353.txt in the run directory. No cite() calls were made because the budget ran out, so the verbatim quotes are recorded in the finding notes but not yet validated in references.bib. Open: q-05 asks for a measured share, either by reading Figs. 12-13 numerically or by running the ADS query.

The 18,660 total, the exclusion of cross-submissions and the Table 1 counts were never validated with cite(), and the cluster share is still the survey's assumption. That leaves three routes to a measured share: reading the extracted keyword and subfield figures of 2602.12303, finding a cluster or ICM concept count in AstroMLab 5, and finding citable bibliometric statements. steps: 1. download_arxiv_full_text for arXiv:2602.12303 with output_dir /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-features/runs/261016_170438 (1 call).

2. read_arxiv_chunk on the Sec. 2.1 dataset description and on the chunk containing Table 1. Record verbatim: (a) the sentence giving 18,660 papers; (b) the sentence excluding replacements and cross-submissions; (c) the Table 1 rows for GA, HE, SR, CO, EP, IM and general. Note the chunk index of each quote. If 18,660 or the exclusion sentence is not found verbatim, report that and withdraw or downgrade f-001 and f-002 rather than restating them (2-4 calls).
3. cite() arXiv:2602.12303 with the validated verbatim quotes from step 2. Only cite text actually seen in the chunk (1-2 calls).

4. get_paper_figures for arXiv:2602.12303. Use only Fig. 12 (most common keywords) and Fig. 13 (top 25 subfields). Read each caption verbatim. Inspect the bars for any entry matching galaxy clusters, clusters of galaxies, ICM, intracluster medium, Sunyaev-Zel'dovich, protoclusters or BCG. If one exists, read its value or estimate it from the axis, with an error of plus or minus one tick. If none is present, record the smallest listed bar value as an upper bound on the cluster keyword count, valid only if 'galaxy clusters' would have qualified for the list (1 call, plus reasoning).

5. Search the remaining 2602.12303 text (1-2 read_arxiv_chunk calls) for any sentence or table mentioning clusters, ICM, SZ, lensing, eROSITA or Euclid with numbers. Also look for 2020-2024 comparison totals for the trend check.

6. download_arxiv_full_text for arXiv:2511.12353, then read_arxiv_chunk (2-3 calls) for: the exact coverage cutoff (July 2025); any per-year paper totals (2020-2025); any concept tied to galaxy clusters, ICM, SZ or cluster lensing, with its paper count; and the ADS keyword table, quoted verbatim. If a cluster concept count exists for all years, divide by 408,590 to get a long-run share, and state that it is an all-years share, not a 2025 share (3-4 calls).
7. cite() arXiv:2511.12353 with verbatim quotes on dataset size, coverage and any cluster-related concept count (1 call).

8. search_arxiv_abstracts, at most 3 queries (e.g. 'bibliometric astronomy subfield growth arXiv', 'galaxy cluster research publication trends', 'astro-ph submission statistics topics'). The aim is a citable source for the fraction of astro-ph.CO or astro-ph.GA papers about clusters, or for growth of cluster papers over time. Use these results as anchors only, never as hit counts. If a promising paper appears, check it with get_arxiv_metadata and read 1 chunk (3-5 calls).

9. Synthesis. Base = 18,660 primary papers, if validated. Strict definition: ICM X-ray and SZ, cluster cosmology and mass calibration, cluster lensing, radio halos and relics, BCG and ICL, protoclusters. Broad definition: strict plus galaxy groups, simulations with cluster analyses, galaxy evolution in clusters, and high-energy or dark-matter searches that use clusters as targets. Exclude star, globular and open clusters, and galaxy 'clustering'. Compute strict and broad counts from the measured share where one exists (figure value, concept share or quoted fraction). Otherwise use the per-category proxy (CO, GA, HE shares times labelled within-category fractions), anchored to any quoted number from steps 4-8. Give the arithmetic, the range and a confidence level. State whether the broad range includes cross-listed gr-qc/hep-ph papers, and if so mark that component as unquantified rather than inventing a figure. Report the trend result, or explicitly 'no per-year data found'. Every number must be tagged either sourced (with arXiv ID and quote) or assumed.
success_criteria: The 18,660 total, the cross-submission exclusion and the Table 1 counts are each either validated with cite() using verbatim quotes, or explicitly withdrawn as not found.
Figs. 12-13 of 2602.12303 are read, with a recorded result: either a numerical value for a cluster-related keyword or subfield, or a stated absence plus an upper bound from the smallest listed bar.
The AstroMLab 5 coverage cutoff and any cluster-related concept count or per-year totals are quoted and cited, or recorded as absent.
The final estimate gives a strict and a broad count, each with explicit arithmetic, a range, and every input labelled sourced or assumed. No web-only number is presented as sourced.
The trend question (2020-2024 compared with 2025) is answered with sourced numbers or explicitly closed as unanswerable with the available sources.
Total tool calls stay within about 23.

result.summary:
Base counts are now cited (f-004); the galaxy-cluster share is still an assumption. Estimate: about 640 strict and about 1,110 broad 2025 galaxy-cluster papers. No source gave a measured cluster share, so the estimate (f-007) is low confidence.

Validated base counts, cited with verbatim quotes (f-004; arXiv:2602.12303, ids tc-...-15/17/25):
- 2025 total: 18,660 astro-ph papers. Replacements and cross-submissions are excluded ('to confine the dataset to only pure Astrophysics papers'). This answers q-01: the base is primary submissions only.
- 2024 total: 16,333, so 2025 is 18,660/16,333 = 1.142, i.e. +14.2%.
- Table 1 primary-subject counts: GA 4761, HE 3869, SR 2958, CO 2789, EP 2293, IM 1722, general 268. 8,684 papers have a secondary subject.

Figs. 12-13 (f-005): Both figures were extracted with captions ('Most Common Keywords for 2025'; 'Top 25 sub-fields and research areas'), but no tool returned bar values. So neither a cluster bar value nor a smallest-bar upper bound could be read.
- The text shows that 'Galaxy Clusters' is not among the top 25 author keywords (Table 8; the last entry is 'High Energy Astrophysics') and not in the top-10 subfields named in the text.
- 'Galaxy Clusters' does exist as a keyword in the taxonomy: Table 7 lists it as the top keyword of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. So q-06 is resolved: cluster papers would have qualified for the list.

AstroMLab 5 (f-006; arXiv:2511.12353, cited): The dataset covers 408,590 papers from 1992 through July 2025. The text gives no per-year totals and no cluster, ICM or SZ concept count. Only example counts appear, e.g. 'galaxies: evolution' 16,321 (5.5%) and 'Gravitational Lensing Surveys' 278. An all-years share cannot be derived without the GitHub concept CSV.

Literature search: two arXiv searches found no citable bibliometric source for a cluster fraction (dead end x-02).

Estimate (f-007, low confidence). Category counts are sourced from Table 1; the within-category fractions are all assumed.
- Strict: 0.12x2789 + 0.04x4761 + 0.03x3869 = 335 + 190 + 116 = 641, i.e. 3.4% of 18,660. Range 443-811.
- Broad: 0.18x2789 + 0.08x4761 + 0.05x3869 + 0.02x1722 = 502 + 381 + 193 + 34 = 1,110, i.e. 5.9%. Range 848-1,413.
- Papers cross-listed into astro-ph from gr-qc or hep-ph are excluded from the base; that addition to the broad count is unquantified.

Trend: There is no sourced per-year cluster data, so the 2020-2024 vs 2025 comparison cannot be answered from these sources. The only sourced growth is in total papers (+14.2%, 2024 to 2025). If the cluster share stayed constant (assumed), 2024 would be about 561 strict and about 972 broad.

questions.text: Does the 2025 total in 2602.12303 count primary astro-ph submissions only, or does it include cross-lists from gr-qc, hep-ph and physics? This difference can change the base by roughly 20-30%.
How should borderline categories be treated: galaxy groups, cluster-scale cosmological simulations, and high-energy or dark-matter searches that use clusters only as targets?
If AstroMLab concept tags cover only January-July 2025, is it valid to scale linearly to the full year, given seasonal submission patterns and large data releases mid-year?
Without a direct ADS or arXiv API facet count, the estimate stays a model-based figure. Note this limitation, and recommend the reproducible ADS query for a later run.

Can the d-02 worker, or a later run, read the numerical values in Figs. 12-13 of arXiv:2602.12303 (look for a 'galaxy clusters' keyword or subfield bar) or run the ADS query abs:("galaxy cluster" OR "clusters of galaxies" OR intracluster) year:2025 collection:astronomy, so that the assumed 5-8% cluster share is replaced by a measured one?

If Fig. 12 or Fig. 13 of 2602.12303 has no galaxy-cluster bar, is an upper bound from the smallest listed bar meaningful? This depends on whether the keyword taxonomy would have produced a 'galaxy clusters' entry at all.
Is an all-years cluster share from AstroMLab 5 (1992 to July 2025) a fair proxy for the 2025 share, given that cluster science may have grown or shrunk relative to exoplanets and transients?
How should borderline categories be counted: galaxy groups, cosmological simulations whose analyses include clusters, and dark-matter or high-energy searches that use clusters only as targets?

The 18,660 base excludes cross-lists. Without an ADS or arXiv-API count, can the gr-qc/hep-ph cross-list contribution be bounded at all, or should it stay an explicitly unquantified addition to the broad estimate?

The reproducible ADS query abs:("galaxy cluster" OR "clusters of galaxies" OR intracluster) year:2025 collection:astronomy, excluding star clusters, remains the recommended direct measurement for a later run with ADS access.

In Table 7 of 2602.12303, 'Galaxy Clusters' is the top keyword of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, yet it is absent from the top 25 keywords overall. Does Fig. 12b (with self-assigned keywords) show a Galaxy Clusters bar whose value can be read visually?

Figs. 12 and 13 were extracted to the run directory but not read numerically. AstroMLab 5 gives only example concepts (e.g. CMB 9,166 papers) and the aggregate for 1992 to July 2025, with no per-year counts and no cluster concept. The ADS keyword table in 2511.12353 lists 'galaxies: evolution' at 5.5% and 'dark matter' at 3.0%, but has no cluster row.

dead_ends.what: Measuring the galaxy-cluster share directly from the text of arXiv:2602.12303 (keyword and subfield counts) and arXiv:2511.12353 (cluster concept counts), plus arXiv abstract searches for bibliometric cluster fractions.
dead_ends.why: 2602.12303 gives no counts for the Fig. 12 and Fig. 13 bars in its text; the figure images were extracted but no tool returned values. 2511.12353 lists only example concepts and keywords, with no cluster or ICM concept and no per-year totals. Two arXiv searches returned no relevant bibliometric source. A measured share needs the AstroMLab GitHub concept CSV, an ADS query, or a visual reading of Fig. 12b.

issues.text: The plan does not fit the 23-call budget. Two full-text downloads, several read_arxiv_chunk passes per paper, possible figure extraction, a conditional external search, six sanity-check queries and multiple cite() calls add up to well over 23. Split the work: d-01 covers 2602.12303 and the final synthesis; the added direction covers 2511.12353 and the independent anchors. Cap the sanity-check queries at about 3.

There is no fallback for the likely case that 2602.12303 gives subfield or category shares but no galaxy-cluster share. Define the proxy now: (astro-ph.CO + astro-ph.GA + astro-ph.HE share) x (cluster fraction within those categories). Also state how the within-category fraction will be justified, for example from a quoted concept or topic table, or failing that as a labelled assumption with a range. Otherwise the final number simply repeats the survey's 5-8% assumption.

The brief asks for a 2020-2024 trend check, and the plan has no step for it. Add one: extract per-year astro-ph totals, and per-year cluster or concept counts if available, from either paper. Use them to test the survey's claim that 2025 was a high-output year, rather than asserting it from the data-release list (eROSITA, Euclid, XRISM).

Strict and broad are not defined well enough to apply to sourced numbers. State in advance which concept or topic labels count as strict (ICM, cluster cosmology, cluster lensing, radio halos and relics, BCG and ICL, protoclusters) and which count as broad (groups, simulations with cluster analyses, high-energy work using clusters as targets). Exclude star, globular and open clusters explicitly. Also note that if source counts include cross-lists, cluster papers listed in both astro-ph.CO and astro-ph.GA must not be counted twice.

The survey's 'just over 1%' OJAp snippet and any arXiv annual-report figure found through web_search cannot be quoted. Either find a citable arXiv source for the 2025 total (2602.12303 is the best candidate) or label the total as unverified. Do not let a web-only number appear as sourced.

Step 4 cannot support any quantitative claim, because search_arxiv_abstracts returns a ranked subset, not hit counts. Keep it out of the arithmetic and report it only as a check of topic breadth and star-cluster contamination.

AstroMLab 5 data ends in July 2025. Scaling January-July to a full year should account for uneven submission rates across the year, with at least a stated +/-10% allowance. Confirm the exact coverage cutoff with get_arxiv_metadata or the text before scaling.

contested.reason: The cited excerpt from tc-261015_2-w1-d-01-15 shows only the title page (chars 0-15000, truncated after the affiliations). It contains neither the 18,660 figure nor the quote on excluding replacements and cross-submissions. The value may well be correct, since it matches the Table 1 sum exactly, but the posted evidence does not show it and no cite() call validated it.

The cited excerpt from tc-261015_2-w1-d-01-17 (chars 35000-55000) shows the telescopes and objects section and the Fig. 2 caption, not Table 1. The per-category counts do not appear in it. The numbers are internally consistent: they sum to 18,660, GA+CO = 7,550 (40.5%), and GA+CO+HE = 11,419 (61.2%). That consistency is not evidence of the source values.

The arithmetic reproduces from the stated assumptions: CO 15-25% gives 418-697, GA 8-12% gives 381-571, HE 3-5% gives 116-193, and others add 30-80, for a total of about 945-1,541. However, the base inputs rest on f-001 and f-002, whose excerpts do not show them. The per-category cluster fractions are unsourced, so the evidence supports none of the cluster-specific content. The broad range of 2,000-3,000 is asserted without any derivation.

issues.text: Quoted values (18,660 and the cross-submission exclusion) are not present in the evidence excerpts. The relevant chunk of 2602.12303 needs to be re-read and passed to cite() so the quote is validated in references.bib.
The Table 1 counts are not in the cited excerpt. The tool call or chunk range containing Table 1 needs to be identified and cited.

The cluster fractions per category (CO 15-25%, GA 8-12%, HE 3-5%) are labelled assumptions with no anchor. The broad range of 2,000-3,000 has no derivation. It also mixes a primary-only base with cross-listed gr-qc and hep-ph papers without quantifying the cross-list contribution. The final number therefore still rests on the survey's unverified 5-8% share.
The 2020-2024 trend check flagged in c-01 was not done. The claim that 2025 was a high-output year for cluster science, driven by eROSITA, Euclid and XRISM, remains unverified.

issues.text: unsupported: A follow-up web search to confirm the snippet failed with a DNS error, so the snippet remains uncitable. — The board records no follow-up web search and no DNS error. It says only that the OJAp snippet is unverified and that web-only numbers cannot be quoted (c-01). This is an invented process event.

unsupported: Each paper has about 10 extracted concepts, clustered into 9,999 concept classes — Neither figure appears on the board. The board gives only the 408,590 papers, the 1992 to July 2025 coverage, example concepts (CMB 9,166) and the public GitHub release.

unsupported: Its stated aim is "a summary of statistics for every paper uploaded onto the Astrophysics arXiv over the past year – 2025". It reports subfield, keyword, country and citation statistics. — The verbatim aim quote is not on the board, and neither are country statistics. The board mentions subfield and keyword breakdowns and citation table 9. The quoted figure captions ("Most Common Keywords for 2025", "Top 25 sub-fields and research areas") are likewise not recorded verbatim.

unsupported: This settles the question of whether cross-lists are included — The finding behind this (f-001) is contested by c-02 because the quote is absent from the evidence excerpts, and q-01 is still marked open on the board. "Settles" overstates it, even though the report adds a verification caveat later.

Step 4's upper bound is weak. A cluster term missing from Fig. 12's top-N list only bounds that exact keyword string, not the share of cluster-topic papers under the strict or broad definition. A paper can be about clusters without carrying the literal keyword, and keyword vocabularies split one topic across many terms (ICM, SZ, cluster lensing). Present the smallest-bar value as a bound on single-keyword frequency only. Do not use it to cap the strict or broad estimate.

Values read off a figure image cannot be passed to cite() as verbatim quotes. Cite the caption text only. Label any bar value as 'figure-read, approximate, plus or minus one tick' in the synthesis, not as a sourced number. If the image is not legible, record 'not readable' rather than estimating a value.

Step 6 has two problems with the AstroMLab 5 concept share. First, concepts are fine-grained and a paper can carry several, so summing several cluster-related concepts double-counts papers. Second, the dataset spans decades, so an all-years share is dominated by older work and may not match the 2025 topic mix. Use only one concept count per estimate, or state that the summed share is an upper bound. Present the result as an independent cross-check on the assumed 4-6%, not as a 2025 measurement.

Step 9's per-category proxy multiplies Table 1 shares by within-category fractions. Those fractions are assumptions and must be labelled as such. The result should not be reported with more precision than about 1,000 papers (range roughly 600-1,500), or the answer will imply a measurement that does not exist. Say explicitly that the arXiv API query in the brief could not be run, so no direct hit count exists.

Reconcile 18,660, the new-submissions-only figure from 2602.12303, with the OJAp-derived figure of about 19,000. These are consistent and their agreement supports the base. Say that the OJAp figure is web-only and is not cited. The brief asks for totals with and without cross-lists. If 2602.12303 gives no cross-list total, record it as not available instead of inferring one.

When scanning Figs. 12-13 and the text, do not count entries for star, globular or open clusters, or for 'clustering', as galaxy-cluster entries. If such entries appear, note them as a check on false positives.

Step 8 (generic bibliometric searches, 3-5 calls) is likely to find little. The worst-case budget is about 20 calls, which is feasible, but if reading 2602.12303 needs more chunks to locate Table 1 or the keyword sections, cut step 8 to 1-2 queries first.

The quoted excerpts are truncated and do not show 18,660, 16,333 or the Table 1 counts verbatim. The character ranges (0-14000 for Sec. 2.1; 28000-42000 for Sec. 3.1 and Table 1) are consistent with the claims, and cite() succeeded, so the finding is accepted. A future synthesis should quote the exact sentences, not just chunk headers.

Arithmetic checks out: 641 (3.4%) strict and 1,111 (5.95%) broad. However, every within-category fraction (0.12, 0.04, 0.03, 0.18, 0.08, 0.05, 0.02) is assumed, and the stated ranges (443-811, 848-1,413) have no documented derivation. Critique c-04 asked that the result not be given more precision than about 1,000 (roughly 600-1,500). The final answer should round accordingly and state that no direct hit count exists. The strict definition also omits IM-primary cluster instrumentation and SZ survey papers; this is a definitional choice that should be stated.

Absence from the top-25 keyword list bounds only the frequency of the literal 'Galaxy Clusters' keyword string, not the topic share (c-04). The Table 7 entry measures institute-paper contributions for one institute, not papers. It should not be used as a lower bound on cluster papers overall.
q-01 and q-06 are marked as resolved in the d-07 summary but remain 'open' on the board. q-02 and q-08 are duplicates. These should be closed or merged before the final write-up.

Query the arXiv API with cat:astro-ph* AND (abs:"galaxy cluster" OR abs:"galaxy clusters" OR abs:"clusters of galaxies" OR abs:intracluster) AND submittedDate:[202501010000 TO 202512312359] and record totalResults.

Run variant queries: add abs:"Sunyaev-Zel'dovich" OR abs:protocluster OR abs:"brightest cluster galaxy" for the broad set, and run the same query for 2024. Note that the API includes cross-lists, unlike the 18,660 base.

Spot-check about 20 returned abstracts for false positives (star or globular clusters, clustering) and for papers that only mention clusters in passing. Apply the measured purity fraction to the totals.
Compare the measured strict and broad counts with f-007's 641 and 1,110, and give a final rounded estimate with a range.
